speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash extend to the baby's diaper area or skin folds, and have you noticed any crusting or oozing? Is there a family history of eczema or asthma in addition to the father's psoriasis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in an infant is highly characteristic of seborrheic dermatitis, often referred to as cradle cap. To rule out other conditions like atopic dermatitis or psoriasis, I need to check if the rash involves other areas. Does the rash extend to the diaper area, skin folds, or behind the ears, and has any topical treatment been tried so far?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead of a 3-month-old infant is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, commonly known as cradle cap.
